principle: Structural depletion operates against false signals of escalation through simultaneous resource removal and tempo acceleration, creating contradiction between what diminishes and what amplifies.

nodes.label: Numerical countdown structure
nodes.description: Systematic reduction from seven samurai to three survivors, with each death functioning as structural phase marker dividing the battle sequence into discrete units rather than continuous action.
evidence: Explicitly tracked across all analytical documents and identified as load-bearing constraint.
Each death divides the 77-minute battle into phases rather than continuous action.
Both the reinforcement system and the depletion-escalation paradox depend on it.

nodes.label: Durational extension of preparation
nodes.description: 60-minute training block with minimal plot advancement, establishing labor investment through repeated similar actions (fence-building, spear practice) with slight variations.
evidence: Dedicated temporal analysis identifies the 60-minute block as temporal accumulation, not plot advancement.
Explicitly linked to making subsequent losses register structurally rather than as spectacle.
Named as prerequisite for the countdown mechanism in validation.

nodes.label: Circular perimeter as tactical map
nodes.description: Stable village geography established through hand-drawn map shown to characters, maintained with spatial consistency throughout battle sequences to allow viewer tracking of tactical positions at specific compass points.
evidence: Detailed spatial analysis: village organized as rough circle with stream, defenders at compass points, attacks from predictable directions.
Named as structural prerequisite for subsequent formal operations, not exposition.
Contradiction analysis shows dependent systems fail when this constraint is breached in the final phase.
rules: Village geography remains spatially consistent across battle sequences

nodes.label: Tempo acceleration across battle phases
nodes.description: Systematic score tempo progression from 80 BPM in first attack to 140 BPM in final attack, creating linear acceleration independent of visual content through percussive rhythmic cells.
evidence: Attack 1 averages ~80 BPM, Attack 2 ~100, Attack 3 ~120, Attack 4 ~140: linear systematic progression.
Percussive score built from 4-8 beat rhythmic cells with no sustained melodic lines.
Validation rates it as reinforcing but not generating the core contradiction.

nodes.label: Hand-drawn village map shown to characters
nodes.description: Diagram of the circular village geography presented to characters, establishing the spatial system the viewer then uses to track tactical positions across the battle.
evidence: Geography is established through a hand-drawn map shown to characters, then maintained with spatial consistency.
Analysis states the map is not exposition but structural prerequisite for subsequent formal operations.

nodes.label: Silence caesuras after each samurai death
nodes.description: 8-15 second passages of no score and minimal ambient sound immediately following each samurai death, marking structural boundaries between battle phases.
evidence: Extended silence occurs immediately after each samurai death, 8-15 seconds.
Silences function as caesuras converting casualties into phase markers.
Validation: important punctuation but countdown operates without it.

nodes.label: Decreasing intervals between bandit attacks
nodes.description: Four bandit attacks arrive at progressively shorter intervals of film time: about 20 minutes between attacks 1 and 2, 15 between 2 and 3, and 8 between 3 and 4.
evidence: Intervals measured as ~20, ~15, and ~8 minutes of film time between successive attacks.
Compression accelerates narrative momentum while maintaining the four-wave structure.

nodes.label: Depth-staging composition across three spatial planes
nodes.description: Action arranged across three or more spatial planes within single frames, compressing multiple narrative threads into unified shots rather than distributing them across montage.
evidence: Foreground, middle-ground, and background layers operate throughout recruitment and battle sequences.
Validation: amplifies spatial efficiency but could be replaced with montage without destroying the work's identity.

nodes.label: Vertical stratification in combat staging
nodes.description: Battle sequences use elevation differences: samurai on rooftops, bandits on lower ground, villagers in doorways at intermediate height, creating three vertical zones of simultaneous action.
evidence: Three vertical zones of action within single frames allow simultaneous tracking of combat threads without cutting.
Analysis: rooftop, ground, and doorway relationships stay consistent across cuts only because the geometry is stable.

nodes.label: Negative space as tactical void
nodes.description: Cleared fields around the village perimeter and vacant streets during attacks function as kill zones where any movement becomes visually salient; the emptiness is functional, not compositional accident.
evidence: Cleared perimeter zones create kill zones where bandits are exposed.
Analysis: voids function predictably only because the circular geometry is known.

nodes.label: Nondiegetic score coverage shift from 17 to 68 percent
nodes.description: Recruitment section carries ~12 minutes of score in 70 minutes (17 percent) with dense ambient sound; battle section carries ~52 minutes of score in 77 minutes (68 percent) with ambient stripped to near-silence.
evidence: Score coverage rises fourfold from recruitment (17 percent) to battle (68 percent).
Correspondence operates at micro-scale: contraction raises score density, expansion reverses it.
Binding allows the viewer to read tactical position through sonic information alone.
rules: Spatial contraction corresponds to score replacing ambient sound

nodes.label: Bandit breach of the perimeter in the final battle phase
nodes.description: In the final phase bandits penetrate the circular perimeter and combat moves to interior spaces, removing the geometric foundation while the film continues using extended takes and depth staging.
evidence: When bandits breach the perimeter, the stable geometry enabling stratification and negative space collapses.
Produces deliberate spatial confusion: viewers cannot track position because the enabling constraint has failed.
rule_violations: Village geography remains spatially consistent across battle sequences

nodes.label: Sonic void at Kikuchiyo's death
nodes.description: At maximum spatial concentration (all defenders at a single point), the film produces near-silence rather than the predicted score density, inverting the spatial-sonic correspondence at structural climax.
evidence: The rule that predicted sonic density through 140 minutes fails at the moment of greatest load.
Analysis: not suspension for emphasis but the system contradicting its own operational logic.
rule_violations: Spatial contraction corresponds to score replacing ambient sound

edges.rationale: Durational investment in preparation makes subsequent subtractions register as structural loss: without the 60-minute labor accumulation, deaths become narrative events rather than structural weight, and the countdown becomes arithmetic rather than tragedy.

Each samurai death triggers an 8-15 second silence caesura that converts the casualty into a phase marker, preventing the countdown from becoming undifferentiated arithmetic; countdown survives without it but loses punctuation.
Each caesura resets the tempo baseline higher, so deaths do not slow the work down but accelerate what remains, feeding the linear tempo progression.
Attack intervals compress as personnel depletes: 20 minutes between attacks 1-2, 15 between 2-3, 8 between 3-4, accelerating momentum while the samurai count decreases.
Depth-staging composition depends on circular perimeter stability: arranging action across three spatial planes requires known geometry to remain spatially coherent across cuts.

Geometric constraint enables tactical legibility: rooftop, ground, and doorway zones maintain the same spatial relationships across cuts only because the circular perimeter is stable; without it vertical staging becomes arbitrary.

Negative space tactics require the stable circular perimeter to function predictably: cleared zones read as kill zones only because the geometry is known; without the constraint the voids lose tactical meaning.
The map shown to characters is not exposition but the warrant establishing the spatial system: it authorizes the viewer to track tactical positions at specific compass points throughout the battle.

Spatial contraction requires sonic replacement: as geography concentrates from dispersed recruitment to circular perimeter, score coverage increases from 17 to 68 percent, letting the viewer read tactical position through sonic information alone.

As resources deplete from seven to three samurai, tempo and tactical effectiveness increase rather than degrade, inverting the expected depletion-capability relationship; the sonic register moves opposite to the numerical register in productive tension.

The final phase systematically violates the enabling condition: bandits breach the perimeter, combat moves to interior spaces where circular logic cannot operate, and the work demonstrates the spatial system's dependency on a condition it then removes.

At Kikuchiyo's death the spatial-sonic rule inverts: maximum spatial concentration produces sonic void rather than predicted score density, contradicting 140 minutes of operational reliability at the moment of greatest structural load.

violated: Village geography remains spatially consistent across battle sequences

failure_modes.consequence: When the circular perimeter fails, the geometric constraint enabling spatial legibility collapses: vertical stratification becomes arbitrary, negative space loses tactical meaning, and extended takes become spatially illegible, producing deliberate spatial confusion.

violated: Spatial contraction corresponds to score replacing ambient sound

failure_modes.consequence: At Kikuchiyo's death maximum spatial concentration produces sonic void rather than predicted score density; the correspondence system contradicts its own operational logic at structural climax, breaking the viewer's ability to read tactical position through sound.

If the escalation register is absent and the viewer tracks only attrition, the structural irony of simultaneous escalation and depletion disappears, reducing the work to simple tragedy; the contradiction between what diminishes and what intensifies becomes invisible.

Without the numerical countdown, the battle's phase structure becomes invisible, the sequence collapses into undifferentiated action, and victory becomes formally indistinguishable from defeat except by the arithmetic fact of survival.

Without the 60-minute labor accumulation, deaths lack structural weight and register as narrative events rather than structural loss; the countdown becomes decorative arithmetic and the depletion-escalation paradox cannot operate.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, the battle becomes undifferentiated action without phase structure; the entire dramatic architecture collapses into generic combat lacking progressive depletion logic.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If removed, deaths lack structural weight because no labor investment is established; the countdown becomes arithmetic rather than tragedy; losses register as narrative events rather than structural
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, spatial coherence collapses; vertical stratification and extended takes become illegible; the viewer cannot track tactical positions and the geometric foundation for formal operations
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the false escalation signal disappears; the contradiction between intensifying tempo and depleting resources collapses into simple attrition narrative without structural irony.
